questions.q: What happens on a third click of a Tableau sort icon?
options: The sort is cleared and the view returns to its default order
The data is permanently deleted
The chart type changes
A new worksheet is created
questions.explain: One click sorts descending, a second sorts ascending, and a third click clears the sort entirely.

questions.q: Does sorting remove any data from the view?
options: No — sorting only reorders the marks that are already there
Yes — sorting always excludes the bottom half of values
Yes — sorting deletes any mark below the average
Sorting removes all null values automatically
questions.explain: Sorting changes the order marks appear in, but it does not include or exclude any data — that's what filters do.

options: A field dragged onto the Filters shelf that includes or excludes values from the view
A sort applied to an axis
A calculated field that always returns TRUE
A type of reference line
questions.explain: A basic filter is created by dragging a field onto the Filters shelf and choosing which values to include or exclude.

questions.q: How does a quick filter differ from a basic filter?
options: A quick filter displays the same filter as a live, interactive card directly on the view or dashboard
A quick filter is faster to compute but otherwise identical in every way
A quick filter can only be applied to calculated fields
A quick filter permanently removes data from the underlying data source
questions.explain: A quick filter takes an existing filter and shows it as a card on the sheet or dashboard, so viewers can change it without editing the workbook.

questions.q: Where does a basic filter live once you've dragged a field onto it?
options: The Filters shelf
The Marks card
The Columns shelf only
The Data pane's calculated fields folder
questions.explain: Any field used to filter the view is dragged onto the Filters shelf, regardless of whether it's also displayed as a quick filter.
